title: A wiki nobody has to be reminded about
goal: You will build a team wiki with a homepage, clear sections, named owners, and a reusable page template.
prerequisites: Names of the people who will own each wiki section

steps.action: Create a new page named "Team Wiki".
steps.where: Left sidebar, "New page" button near the bottom.
steps.why: This page will be the central entrance to the wiki.
steps.checkpoint: You should see an empty page titled "Team Wiki" in the main window and in the left sidebar.
hint_levels: Start in the left sidebar.
Use the New page button, then replace Untitled with the wiki name.
Click New page, click the Untitled title field, type Team Wiki, and press Enter.

steps.action: Add a short welcome sentence explaining what belongs in the wiki.
steps.where: Main page editor directly below the "Team Wiki" title.
steps.why: A clear purpose helps teammates know when to use the wiki.
steps.checkpoint: You should see a sentence below the page title describing the wiki's purpose.
hint_levels: Click beneath the title.
Type one sentence such as: Find our processes, policies, and team knowledge here.
Click the first empty block below Team Wiki, type Find our processes, policies, and team knowledge here, and press Enter.

steps.where: Empty block in the main page editor; slash-command menu opened by typing "/page".
steps.why: A Company section gives shared information a predictable home.
steps.checkpoint: You should see a page block named "Company" on the Team Wiki homepage and a nested Company page in the left sidebar.
hint_levels: Use a page block beneath the welcome sentence.
The /page command creates a page inside the current page.
Click an empty block, type /page, choose Page from the menu, type Company, and press Enter.

steps.where: Team Wiki main page editor, in a new empty block below the Company page block.
steps.why: This section provides one home for onboarding, benefits, and team norms.
steps.checkpoint: You should see separate "Company" and "People & Culture" page blocks on the homepage.
hint_levels: Add another page block below Company.
Open the slash-command menu and choose Page again.
Press Enter below Company, type /page, click Page, type People & Culture, and press Enter.

steps.action: Create a subpage named "How We Work".
steps.where: Team Wiki main page editor, in a new empty block below the People & Culture page block.
steps.why: This section keeps recurring processes and working agreements easy to find.
steps.checkpoint: You should see three section page blocks: Company, People & Culture, and How We Work.
hint_levels: Repeat the page-block pattern once more.
Create a Page block in the empty line below People & Culture.
Press Enter below People & Culture, type /page, click Page, type How We Work, and press Enter.

steps.action: Add an inline table database named "Wiki Directory" to the homepage.
steps.where: Team Wiki main page editor; slash-command menu opened with "/table" and the "Table view" option under Databases.
steps.why: The directory gives teammates one searchable list of wiki pages and their owners.
steps.checkpoint: You should see a database table titled "Wiki Directory" embedded on the Team Wiki page.
hint_levels: Add the directory below the section links.
Choose the database-style Table view, not a simple table block.
Click an empty block below the sections, type /table, select Table view under Databases, choose New database if prompted, and name it Wiki Directory.

steps.action: Rename the database's second column to "Owner" and change its property type to "Person".
steps.where: Wiki Directory table, second column header menu, "Edit property" panel, "Type" menu.
steps.why: A Person property makes responsibility visible and assignable.
steps.checkpoint: You should see an "Owner" column with person-shaped cells or an "Add person" prompt.
hint_levels: Open the menu on the second column header.
Edit that property's name and select Person as its type.
Click the second column header, click Edit property, change the name to Owner, open Type, and click Person.

steps.action: Add one directory row for each section and assign an owner in every row.
steps.where: Wiki Directory table, "New" rows in the first column and cells in the "Owner" column.
steps.why: Visible ownership tells everyone who maintains each part of the wiki.
steps.checkpoint: You should see rows for Company, People & Culture, and How We Work, each with a person's name in the Owner column.
hint_levels: Use the table rows to list the three sections and their maintainers.
Enter each section name in the first column, then choose a workspace member in Owner.
Click New, type Company, click its Owner cell, choose a person, and repeat for People & Culture and How We Work.

steps.action: Create a database template named "Standard Wiki Page" with headings for "Summary", "Details", and "Related Links".
steps.where: Wiki Directory database, dropdown arrow beside the blue "New" button, "New template" option, template page editor.
steps.why: A shared template makes future wiki pages consistent and quicker to write.
steps.checkpoint: You should see "Standard Wiki Page" listed in the New button's template menu, and its editor should display the three headings.
hint_levels: Look beside the database's New button for its template menu.
Create a new template, name it, then add three Heading 2 blocks.
Click the arrow beside New, click New template, name it Standard Wiki Page, then type /heading 2 and add Summary, Details, and Related Links as separate headings.
